title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with synthetic media. A WhatsApp video call presented a face and a voice resembling Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay, and the caller used that appearance to promise financial aid and then to demand payments. The failure is not a model stating something false in text. It is a fabricated person used in a live call to move money.

The point of failure is the call itself. A video call on a consumer messaging app presents a face and a voice as evidence of who is speaking, and nothing in that channel tests the claim. Catching it would have taken confirmation through a route independent of the call, because the requests themselves, processing fees, exchange charges, a PIN unlock and a supposed CBI fine, were the only thing on offer. Police advised people not to trust such calls or to pay on them.

What is not established is who made the call, whether that person produced the deepfake, or that anyone will be held responsible, and a case registered under the Information Technology Act is not a finding.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru, Ratikanta Giri, received a WhatsApp video call on Sept 9 from someone using a deepfake to look and sound like Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid and said a manager would handle the transfer. The fraudster then demanded processing fees and other payments. Giri paid over Rs 1.04 lakh through a digital payment app.

The demands included Rs 5,000 as exchange charges, Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN, and more than Rs 50,000 as a supposed CBI fine. When another Rs 50,000 was demanded, Giri refused and realized he had been duped. He contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then Byappanahalli police. A case was registered under the Information Technology Act. Police urged people not to trust such calls or make payments based on them.
